subject: Standardizing a legend for an animation

messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Standardizing a legend for an animation
parts:
A good (pacific time zone) afternoon to all,

I have become interested lately in using animations to demonstrate a
particular trend over time. So I have used for() to loop through dates
outputting a jpeg for a particular date. Then you gather all those
jpeg into an .avi file or .mpeg of whatever. Basically I am drawing
from this post:

http://www.drewconway.com/zia/?p=2800

My problem is with the legends. I am at a loss as to how to
standardize a legend to so that when making the animation the values
in the legend don't change. In the example below the "val" variable
controls the size of the points. I thought that I could set the limits
of the legend using scale_size but that doesn't seem to work. In the
example below, 3 jpegs are generate and scrolling through them, you
can see that the legend jumps around which isn't ideal if one was
trying to make a clean animation.

Any idea on how I can set the legend limit based on the complete
dataset rather than just to the particular sequence in the loop?
Example below.

Thanks so much in advance!

Sam

library(ggplot2)
library(scales)


set.seed(11)
df <- rbind(data.frame(x=runif(10,1,4), y=1:10,
Date=seq(as.Date("2011-05-03","%Y-%m-%d"),by="day", length=10),
fac=factor("Group1")),
data.frame(x=runif(10,1,4), y=2:11,

Date=seq(as.Date("2011-05-03","%Y-%m-%d"),by="day", length=10),
fac=factor("Group2"))
)
df$val <- runif(20, 9,10)

## All the points
ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y))+
geom_point(aes(size=val, colour=fac))

## A loop to generate frame for the animation. One frame for one day.
for (i in seq(as.Date("2011-05-03","%Y-%m-%d"), by="day", length=3)) {
plt <- ggplot(df[df$Date==i,], aes(x=x, y=y)) +
geom_point(aes(size=val, colour=fac)) +
scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 12)) +
scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 4)) +
scale_size(range=c(9,10)) +
opts(title=paste(df[df$Date==i,]$Date))
jpeg(paste("WD", i, ".jpg", sep=""), width = 780, height = 480, quality=100)
print(plt)
dev.off()
}

messages.author: d31339b95f6e694c
messages.subject: Re: Standardizing a legend for an animation
parts:
On 2012-Apr-12, at 23:03 , Sam Albers wrote:
>
> I thought that I could set the limits
> of the legend using scale_size but that doesn't seem to work.

limits work for me.

range is the range of the *size* of the UI elements (the points), not of the data. So you should either leave it alone or use something other than c(9,10) which results in points of very similar size.

limits is the argument that controls the limits of the data that is represented.

So you want:
scale_size(range=c(5,10), limits=c(9,10)) +
or possibly
scale_size(limits=c(9,10), breaks=c(9, 9.5, 10)) +
or the more versatile
scale_size(limits=c(min(df$val), max(df$val))) +
